archetype.name: Rookie Developmental (emergency QB3)
archetype.definition: A seventh-round rookie third-stringer who was pushed into a game because of injuries ahead of him, with a willingness to throw deep and into tight windows but no offensive structure built around him yet.

report.headline: One forced debut: deep shots worked, but almost nothing else did.
report.take:
Kaliakmanis is Washington's QB3, a 223rd overall pick who was never meant to see the field in October. He did in Week 4 because the quarterback room fell apart. Jayden Daniels started the first three games, Marcus Mariota started against Indianapolis and went down with a sprained MCL, and Kaliakmanis played 84% of the snaps in a 30-13 loss as a 4.5-point underdog. Everything below comes from one game and 36 dropbacks, played mostly in relief by a player who probably took few, if any, first-team practice reps that week. Read it that way.

The outline of his game is still visible. He hunted the ball downfield: his intended air yards were 12.9, a third of his throws went into tight windows, and 9 of his 33 attempts traveled 20+ yards. Only two of those deep throws were completed, but one went for a touchdown, and that bucket was his only positive one at +0.20 EPA. Short throws were efficient as completions (12 of 14) but produced roughly zero EPA and included his interception. The real damage came in between and behind the line: 0 for 4 at 10-19 yards and 1 for 6 on throws behind the line of scrimmage. Missing that badly on screens and swings usually means timing and rhythm problems with receivers he hasn't practiced with, not a lack of arm.

The numbers also hide some context. He held the ball 3.04 seconds and was hit or sacked on 23.5% of dropbacks, yet was sacked only once. That points to a player who stands in and takes hits to throw rather than eating sacks, which is a decent sign for a rookie. His better EPA came while trailing by 9 or more (-0.07 versus -0.51 in one-score situations), so part of the production came against a soft, protect-the-lead defense. Third down was the clearest failure: one conversion in 10 tries at an average of 8.9 yards to go. Losing Terry McLaurin and the right guard, Sam Cosmi, contributed, and his two most-targeted receivers, Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams, combined for 16 targets at clearly negative EPA.

Where it's heading is mostly out of his hands. Dan Quinn is aiming for Daniels to practice fully and start against the Giants, and Mariota is doubtful. The likeliest outcome is that Kaliakmanis goes back to a backup role, probably as the No. 2 while Mariota heals. His value this year is as insurance. One rough relief outing doesn't tell us whether he can handle a full week of game planning.

strengths.title: Willing and able downfield
strengths.body: He kept testing coverage deep even as the game slipped away, and the 20+ yard bucket was the only one with positive EPA, including his touchdown. That aggressiveness fits his air-yards profile and is a trait worth developing. The 2-for-9 hit rate on deep throws, though, is a coin-flip sample, not a skill measurement.

strengths.title: Takes hits instead of sacks
strengths.body: He was hit or sacked on nearly a quarter of his dropbacks but sacked on only 2.9% of them, which ranks 5th of 42. With a starting guard out, that suggests he gets the ball out under duress rather than taking negative plays. Over a bigger sample, his long time to throw would probably push that sack rate up.

strengths.title: Accurate on the short stuff
strengths.body: He completed 12 of 14 throws under 10 air yards, 17 points above expected. The basic reads and throws were there. The problem was that those completions didn't produce any value.

concerns.title: Accuracy collapsed outside short range
concerns.body: He finished 11.85 points below expected completion percentage, 40th of 42 qualifiers. He went 0 for 4 at intermediate depth and 1 for 6 behind the line. The screen misses look like timing problems with an unfamiliar receiver group, which can improve with reps. The intermediate misses are the bigger long-term question for a late-round passer.

concerns.title: Couldn't sustain drives on third down
concerns.body: One conversion in 10 third-down plays, at -1.07 EPA per play, sank the offense. The long average distance (8.9 yards) reflects a team that was already behind schedule, but his interception and the one sack both came on third down.

concerns.title: Worse when the game was competitive
concerns.body: His EPA was -0.51 per play in one-score situations against -0.07 while trailing by 9 or more. The better numbers came against a defense that was content to give up yards, so the full-game totals somewhat flatter him.

trend.note: One appearance, in relief, after Mariota went down in Week 4. There is no path to read yet, only a single uneven outing.

nextGame.headline: Daniels expected back; Kaliakmanis likely returns to the bench
nextGame.body:
If he did play, the Giants would be an odd fit for his profile. Their pass rush is the weakest in the league by sack rate and 31st in hit rate, so he would get the clean pockets his 3-second drop-backs need. But they are 3rd-best against deep passes, which shuts down the one area that worked for him. They also run the ball more than almost anyone, 10 points under expected pass rate, which shortens games and limits possessions.

Availability decides everything here. Quinn wants Daniels to practice fully and start, and Mariota is doubtful with an MCL sprain, so Kaliakmanis projects as the active backup rather than the starter. McLaurin, Cosmi and Rachaad White are all listed out but tied to a Week 5 return estimate, which would help whoever plays quarterback. On the New York side, safety Jason Pinnock (concussion) and edge Chauncey Golston (neck) are questionable. That would thin an already weak rush and a secondary that has been strong against deep throws.

keyMatchups.title: Clean pockets against a weak rush
keyMatchups.body: New York ranks last in sack rate and 31st in hit rate. For a passer who holds the ball and took hits on almost a quarter of his dropbacks, that is the most favorable part of the matchup. With Golston questionable, the rush could be thinner still.

keyMatchups.title: His deep game against a deep-ball wall
keyMatchups.body: His only positive bucket was 20+ yards. The Giants allow -0.28 EPA on deep passes, 3rd in the league, and rank 6th in explosive pass rate allowed. He would have to win underneath, where his completions produced little.

keyMatchups.title: Who takes the snaps
keyMatchups.body: Daniels started the first three weeks and is targeted to return, while Mariota is doubtful. Kaliakmanis only plays if Daniels has a setback or exits during the game.

nextGame.watch: Daniels' practice participation through the week. A full Wednesday session essentially rules out Kaliakmanis playing.

restOfSeason.body: Expect very little volume. With Daniels returning and Mariota's timeline undetermined, Kaliakmanis is a backup who plays only if the injuries pile up again. If he is pressed into a start, a full week of first-team practice should fix much of the screen and timing mess, and his short-area accuracy should carry over. A 45% completion rate is too low to persist even for a rookie QB3. His deep touchdown production would likely fade, and with a long time to throw, his sack rate would climb toward something more normal.

confidence.note: One relief game, 36 dropbacks, and no career history; he is likely back on the bench next week.
